first.rationale: I intend to test onboarding simplification because completion and activation are both deteriorating, while verifying its durability and the qualified-revenue effects of promotional pricing. Pricing is highly consequential given competitor pressure, but its inherited evidence is framed around acquisition and revenue lift rather than sustainable qualified revenue. Use a guarded standard experiment rather than a broad rollout until the archived records are reviewed.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The archived record confirms improved completion, faster time-to-value, and a 3% lift in 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Do not pursue targeted promotional pricing this cycle: despite an 18% qualified-revenue lift, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Treat pricing as a short-term acquisition lever with material downstream value risk, not as the primary growth action.

final2.rationale: Continue the already selected onboarding-simplification experiment rather than switching to targeted discounts. It directly addresses the current completion and activation problems and has confirmed improvement in time-to-value and 30-day retention. The deeper competitor price cut increases pressure, but the verified discount record shows a 12% retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle, creating unacceptable sustainable-revenue risk. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and evaluate pricing separately when verification capacity returns.
